newsitem.title: USA: PRESS DIGEST - New York Times front page- May 7.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - New York Times front page- May 7.

text.p: The New York Times reported the following stories on its front page Wednesday:
* Britain's newly-elected Labour government gave control over interest rates to the country's central bank, the Bank of England.
* Milwaukee is drawing attention as the first city to enforce strict rules seen by the new Federal welfare law, with critics arguing the system penalizes the poor but others claiming success.
* New York City Mayor Rudolph Giuliani said his next budget would include a tax cut package for residents of New York City.
* A former member of the Heaven's Gate cult was found dead in a California hotel room in a suicide resembling the group's earlier and nearby mass suicide, authorities said.

* President Bill Clinton and Mexican President Ernesto Zedillo ended two days of meeting in Mexico by signing joint statements agreeing to intensify the war on drugs and cooperate on border migration problems.
* U.S. professional basketball team Boston Celtics hired University of Kentucky coach Rick Pitino as its coach and made him the highest-paid coach in sports.
* A jury in North Carolina did not give the death penalty to Thomas Richard Jones, sentencing him to life in prison without parole for homicides caused by impaired driving.
* Many in Hong Kong worry about China's attitude towards contractual agreements, as it awaits imminent takeover.
